validation.criterion: error vs a float64 ground truth no larger than 1.1x the reference's own error

deviations.what: RMSNorm computes in float32 with the float32 epsilon for every input dtype
deviations.why: torch.nn.RMSNorm(eps=None) does this (verified bit-exact for bf16). The spec assumed finfo(input dtype).eps, which for bf16 is 0.0078 and changed outputs by up to 90% in a test.

deviations.what: rotary and timestep frequencies are computed in float64 and rounded once to float32; long-position parity is judged against a float64 ground truth instead of torch CPU bits
deviations.why: torch CPU float32 exp is off by one ulp for 667 of the frequencies checked and torch CUDA differs again; at position ~2000 or t ~1000 one ulp of frequency is one ulp of the angle (~6e-5). The port's error vs float64 is no larger than the reference's (5.4e-5 vs 6.3e-5 for the timestep embedding). Recorded small-position calls match at <= 1.2e-7.

follow_ups: bf16 parity of attention and blocks is measured in spec 05 stage B against the float32 reference.
Spec 04 builds blocks on these primitives; dit_cases.replay_calls is reused there.
